patterns_data.top_pattern: Authorization coding shifts are masking true inpatient spend drivers
patterns_data.what_is_impacting: Commercial Local Group authorization coding across CA, VA, NY, and OH
key_driver_codes: Postpartum and Postabortion Diagnoses without O.R. Procedures
patterns_data.pattern_details: A large share of the apparent inpatient increase is tied to authorization code redistribution rather than a clean utilization or reimbursement signal. The issue is heaviest in CA and also appears in VA, NY, and OH, touching ungroupable, spine, and postpartum claims. Validate PA-required coding and claim mapping before taking utilization or rate action.
patterns_data.why_it_matters: If this coding issue is not corrected first, UM, network, and reimbursement actions may target the wrong root cause.
patterns_data.recommended_next_step: Run a joint UM and data-quality audit of PA-required coding, remap AUTH_CODE_DISTRIBUTION records, and confirm how affected inpatient claims are classified before changing policy or provider rates.
patterns_data.validation_reason: The identified spend is explicitly flagged as an auth or mapping shift that requires validation before action.
evidence_summary: CA authorization code redistribution accounts for about +$7.2M, led by ungroupable (+$4.6M), cervical spinal fusion (+$1.8M), and postpartum claims (+$0.8M).
VA adds about +$1.5M of the same issue, concentrated at HENRICO DOCTORS' HOSPITAL.
NY and OH add about +$1.0M more, mostly tied to OHIO STATE UNIVERSITY WEXNER MEDICAL CENTER and THE CLEVELAND CLINIC MAIN CAMPUS.

patterns_data.top_pattern: CT PPO acute spend is concentrated at Yale New Haven with both more admits and higher paid per admit
patterns_data.what_is_impacting: Commercial Local Group PPO acute hospitals in CT
patterns_data.pattern_details: CT PPO inpatient growth is heavily concentrated at YALE NEW HAVEN HOSPITAL. Both authorization-required and non-authorization acute admissions increased, and paid per admit also rose, pointing to combined volume and reimbursement pressure rather than a single coding issue. This is a provider-focused cost trend with clear UM and network levers.
patterns_data.why_it_matters: A single acute hospital appears to be driving a large share of CT inpatient cost growth, making this a high-value target for provider-specific action.
patterns_data.recommended_next_step: Launch a joint provider review for YALE NEW HAVEN HOSPITAL covering admission growth, level of care, authorization pathways, and contract performance for CT PPO acute stays.
evidence_summary: Authorization-required CT PPO acute claims at YALE NEW HAVEN HOSPITAL added about +$4.2M on 41 more admissions, with paid per admit up about $7.1K.
Non-authorization CT PPO acute claims added another +$1.1M on 50 more admissions, with paid per admit up about $3.1K.
The pattern is concentrated in one provider and one facility setting rather than spread broadly across CT.

patterns_data.what_is_impacting: Commercial Local Group PPO acute hospitals in OH
key_driver_codes: OHIO STATE UNIVERSITY WEXNER MEDICAL CENTER
patterns_data.pattern_details: OH PPO acute spend is rising across two academic centers, but the mechanism differs by provider. THE CLEVELAND CLINIC MAIN CAMPUS is primarily a volume story, while OHIO STATE UNIVERSITY WEXNER MEDICAL CENTER shows both higher admissions and modest paid-per-admit pressure. This should be handled as a provider concentration issue, not a broad marketwide hospital trend.
patterns_data.why_it_matters: Targeting the two named providers can address most of the OH PPO acute increase more efficiently than a broad statewide intervention.
patterns_data.recommended_next_step: Set up provider-specific action plans for THE CLEVELAND CLINIC MAIN CAMPUS and OHIO STATE UNIVERSITY WEXNER MEDICAL CENTER, pairing admission management with contract and payment performance review.
evidence_summary: THE CLEVELAND CLINIC MAIN CAMPUS added about +$2.3M on 47 more admissions, while paid per admit fell about $6.6K, confirming a volume-led trend.
OHIO STATE UNIVERSITY WEXNER MEDICAL CENTER added about +$1.7M on 22 more admissions, with paid per admit up about $5.1K.
Medical Back Problems without MCC added another +$0.2M on 8 more admissions within the same OH PPO acute setting.

patterns_data.top_pattern: CA acute hospital spend is rising across PPO and HMO inpatient business
patterns_data.what_is_impacting: Commercial Local Group acute hospitals in CA
key_driver_codes: Postpartum and Postabortion Diagnoses without O.R. Procedures
patterns_data.pattern_details: CA acute hospital spend is increasing across Commercial PPO and HMO inpatient business. PPO acute claims show both more admissions and higher paid per admit, while additional PPO utilization in postpartum and back cases is mostly volume-led. A smaller HMO acute component is driven by very high paid per admit on aftercare cases.
patterns_data.why_it_matters: CA has a broad inpatient hospital cost trend that spans both utilization management and reimbursement levers.
patterns_data.recommended_next_step: Prioritize CA inpatient UM and reimbursement review for PPO acute admissions, with focused claim review on ungroupable, spine, postpartum, and aftercare cases before expanding broader policy changes.
evidence_summary: CA PPO acute mixed pressure added about +$3.0M, including ungroupable claims at +$2.4M on 5 more admissions and cervical spinal fusion at +$0.5M on 5 more admissions.
Additional CA PPO utilization added about +$0.5M, led by postpartum cases on 20 more admissions and back cases on 7 more admissions, with paid per admit roughly flat to down.
CA HMO acute claims added about +$0.3M from aftercare cases despite 1 fewer admission, with paid per admit up about $189.2K.

patterns_data.top_pattern: Post-acute facility use is creating high-cost pressure in GA, VA, and WI
patterns_data.what_is_impacting: Commercial Local Group post-acute facilities in GA, VA, and WI

impact_summary.volume_signal: flat to up from a small base

patterns_data.pattern_details: Post-acute settings are generating outsized cost pressure, especially in long term care hospitals. GA is almost entirely a unit-cost story with no admission growth, while VA and WI add more spend through a small number of very expensive LTCH and rehab admissions. This points to a site-of-care and reimbursement issue more than broad acute-hospital utilization.
patterns_data.why_it_matters: Very high paid per admit in post-acute settings can create rapid spend growth even when volume is flat or only modestly higher.
patterns_data.recommended_next_step: Review LTCH and rehab authorization criteria, level-of-care decisions, and contract terms for the cited products and states, starting with GA and VA.
patterns_data.validation_reason: Several drivers come from very small numbers of admissions, including ungroupable LTCH claims, so claim-level confirmation should precede broad policy changes.
evidence_summary: GA POS LTCH added about +$2.5M with no admission growth and paid per admit up about $1.3M.
VA POS LTCH added about +$1.1M on 6 more admissions, with paid per admit up about $181.7K.
VA PPO LTCH added about +$0.4M on 2 more admissions, and WI physical rehab added about +$0.3M on 4 more admissions with paid per admit up about $82.4K.

patterns_data.top_pattern: Maternity and NICU complications are creating small-volume, high-cost spikes in CA and VA
patterns_data.what_is_impacting: Maternity and NICU inpatient episodes in CA and VA
key_driver_codes: Full Term Neonate with Major Problems
Extreme Immaturity or Respiratory Distress Syndrome, Neonate
Vaginal Delivery without Sterilization or D&C without CC/MCC
patterns_data.pattern_details: Maternity and NICU cost pressure is coming from a small number of high-acuity neonatal and maternal complication cases, not broad delivery volume alone. The largest spikes involve neonatal respiratory complications and a C-section-linked NICU episode, with additional CA maternal complication activity in pre-eclampsia and postpartum infection. This should be handled as a focused maternity and neonatal case review.
patterns_data.why_it_matters: Maternity and NICU cases need different clinical, UM, and provider actions than general Med/Surg admissions.
patterns_data.recommended_next_step: Send these episodes to maternity and neonatal clinical review to confirm severity, delivery pathway, NICU admission appropriateness, and any case-rate or outlier payment terms.
patterns_data.validation_reason: The increase is driven by small numbers of high-cost maternal and neonatal cases, so claim-level validation is needed before broader policy action.
evidence_summary: A CA NICU case at LUCILE PACKARD CHILDRENS HOSPITAL STANFORD added about +$0.9M on 1 admission for a neonate with major problems.
A VA NICU pattern at HENRICO DOCTORS' HOSPITAL added about +$0.4M across 5 admissions tied to extreme immaturity or respiratory distress and C-section delivery.
CA maternal complications added about +$0.6M more, including a rare vaginal delivery case at +$0.3M and severe pre-eclampsia cases at +$0.2M on 16 more admissions.
